content.text: 9-Year-Old Girl Found Dead In Tote Along River; Grandma Among 4 Charged In ‘Severe Abuse’ Case Two more adults have been charged months after a 9-year-old girl was found dead in a tote along the Youghiogheny River, as prosecutors say they allowed “severe child abuse and neglect” to continue inside a Fayette County home, authorities announced on Tuesday, April 21. 04/22/2026 7:30 a.m. Theresa Marie Shipley, 63, identified as the child’s grandmother, and Sandra Lynn Umensetter, 51, a family friend, were charged in connection with the prolonged abuse that led to the death of 9-year-old Renesmay Eutsey, Fayette County District Attorney Mike Aubele said.Both women face charges of endangering the welfare of children and recklessly endangering another person, and Shipley also faces a charge for failing to report suspected child abuse, the DA said.They were arraigned on Tuesday, April 21, and committed to Fayette County Prison after failing to post $100,000 bail, court records show. Their preliminary hearing is scheduled for Wednesday, April 29, court records show. The charges were filed after investigators received an autopsy report and additional records from the Westmoreland County Coroner’s Office, Aubele said.Those findings confirmed Renesmay died from malnourishment, neglect, and blunt force trauma injuries, the DA said. The injuries were consistent with those suffered by a 7-year-old child in the home who survived but required hospitalization, Aubele said. Cell phone analysis showed Theresa Shipley and Umensetter were caring for the children during multiple time periods in the months leading up to Renesmay’s death, investigators said.“In short, the children in the home were subjected to severe child abuse and neglect over a long period of time,” Aubele said. “These two defendants were present for it and supervised these children during the times they were severely abused; they did nothing to help them.” The new charges significantly expand a case that first shocked the region in early September.The Abuse Discovery That Sparked The Death Penalty FilingFour children were removed from the Third Street home in Dunbar Borough on the day the homicide investigation began. A medical evaluation revealed a 6-year-old child suffering from severe neglect with a growth rate at the 0th percentile, prompting immediate hospitalization, officials said. The child remains in stable condition. Three other children were placed in foster care outside Fayette County, the DA said.The Missing Child Call That Became A Murder CaseThe case began as a missing child investigation when troopers were called to the home at 12:41 p.m. on Wednesday, Sept. 3, 2025, after Renesmay was reported missing, police said. Sarah Shipley, who lived in the home, told investigators she put the children to bed around 2:30 a.m. and was woken around noon to find the girl gone, investigators said. She claimed another child mentioned the girl had talked about running away and said the bedroom window was cracked open, police said. But surveillance video later showed a vehicle arriving at 3:53 a.m., with someone entering and exiting the home multiple times, according to investigators.Children Reveal What Really HappenedWhen Children & Youth Services interviewed the children, one broke down crying and apologized for lying, saying, “I’m never going to see my baby sister again because she’s in heaven,” according to police paperwork. Another child told troopers their mother, Kourtney Malinda Eutsey, killed Renesmay and placed her in a tote, investigators said.A sibling said the last time she saw Renesmay alive was around 10 p.m. Tuesday when she heard her screaming and crying, investigators said. She said she overheard Eutsey and Shipley planning to take the girl “to a river far, far away” and later saw her inside a black garbage bag placed into a tote, police said. Confession And River DumpingKourtney Eutsey later admitted to placing the child’s body in a garbage bag and tote before dumping it along the Youghiogheny River near Smithton, troopers said.She led investigators to the location around 3:30 a.m., where Renesmay was found partially submerged, police said.Eutsey told investigators the child had burned her back in a bathtub a week earlier and never received medical care, court documents said. She said the girl vomited and began choking Tuesday night and that she attempted CPR for 30 minutes but did not call 911 because she feared getting into trouble, investigators said. Signs Of Prolonged AbuseRenesmay weighed just 45 pounds and had bruises, cigarette burns, and signs of severe malnourishment, the DA said.“It’s very apparent that this girl suffered,” Aubele said.Charges Against The Original DefendantsKourtney Eutsey and Sarah Shipley were both charged with criminal homicide and related offenses following the investigation, court records show. Eutsey faces charges including criminal homicide, aggravated assault, abuse of a corpse, tampering with evidence, and concealing the death of a child, filings show. Her preliminary arraignment was held on Thursday, Sept. 4, and she was denied bail, resulting in her being held in custody, court records show. Eutsey is scheduled for a pre-trial conference on April 29, with trial set to begin May 4, court records show.Sarah Shipley faces charges including criminal homicide, conspiracy, aggravated assault of a child under 13, abuse of a corpse, tampering with evidence, and concealing the death of a child, court records show. Her preliminary arraignment was held in early September, resulting in her being held in custody, filings show. A status hearing is set for June 11, with trial scheduled to begin July 6, court records show.Both women pleaded not guilty during a preliminary hearing in November and remain jailed awaiting trial, according to court records. Prosecutors have filed notices of aggravated circumstances, making both eligible for the death penalty if convicted of first-degree murder, Aubele said. Biological Mother SpeaksRenesmay’s biological mother, Christina Benedetto, said she had not seen her daughter in four years after losing custody, Benedetto told reporters. She said Eutsey, a blood relative, had also been caring for her three other children, Benedetto said.“Before she went with them, she had so much light in her eyes,” Benedetto said. “Instead of saying they couldn’t handle her anymore, they chose the worst possible thing,” she said. “Why put her in a tote, in a garbage bag, and throw her away like she didn’t mean anything? She meant everything to us,” Benedetto said.The Investigation ContinuesThe investigation remains ongoing as prosecutors continue to review evidence and pursue additional charges, Aubele said.
